rubrics.criterion: Evaluation of declared response conditions (the key=value operators tested by the engine's action lookup) is performed by the response objects' own class hierarchy rather than by orchestration code reading the response's code/size/time/message/content-length fields.
rubrics.rationale: This instance displaced the whole condition dispatch that response classes previously answered for their own state; restoring it behind the response hierarchy is the central outcome of the task.

rubrics.criterion: Presentation of a result as data — the values that result rows, the CSV/XML/runtime records and the names of saved dumps are built from — is answered by the response objects themselves, so the logging pipeline receives those values by asking each response instead of unpacking its fields.
rubrics.rationale: The row and dump-naming duties were moved into free functions of the reporting pipeline that discriminate between response kinds themselves; the repair must put this derived-from-own-data behavior back with the data owners in this single-module codebase.

rubrics.criterion: Per-worker progress records themselves now perform the bookkeeping on their own counters: hit/fail/skip/retry/ignore transitions and the current-candidate/timing-ring updates are applied through the record's own members, and the engine no longer assigns or increments the record's counter fields from outside.
rubrics.rationale: The counters moved into per-worker records precisely so that third-party accounting sites in the engine could be collapsed; if the record remains a passive field bag mutated externally, the instance's core ownership problem is unresolved.

rubrics.criterion: The summary aggregation (per-worker totals folded into the end-of-run report) and the interactive monitor's per-worker line obtain their data through the record's interface rather than by reading the record's counter and current-candidate fields directly.
rubrics.rationale: These two read paths are the instance's read-only manifestations of the same displaced ownership; fixing only the write path would leave the engine's readers coupled to the record's layout.

rubrics.criterion: The hidden analysis for this instance's misplaced-behavior relation reports no remaining matches on the repaired tree (no function or method outside an object's own class reaching deeply into that object's project-owned instance data through a parameter).
rubrics.rationale: The relation this task was built around is measurable by the task's own detector; this anchors the grade to the relation itself rather than to any particular repair shape, so any behavior-preserving repair that satisfies the relation passes.

rubrics.criterion: Every call path that used to invoke the displaced implementations was consistently rewired to request the restored services: the engine's action lookup, the consumer-report processing in the engine, the summary aggregation, the monitor's wait-state rendering, and the logging pipeline's result and saved-response branches all go through the new owner interfaces.
rubrics.rationale: This instance displaced behavior along a multiprocess pipeline with seven distinct call sites; a repair that moves the behavior but leaves one caller bypassing its new owner would silently strand a code path and regress that path's output.

rubrics.criterion: The dispatch the engine relies on to ask a response about a condition routes transparently for every response kind the framework produces, including plain (base-class) result objects used by modules such as the finger, dns or ike modules, and condition availability still follows each kind's declared capabilities.
rubrics.rationale: In this framework several protocol modules produce response objects that are not the HTTP subclass; a repair that only handles the HTTP shape of the restored interface breaks the plug-in modules it was supposed to keep compatible.

rubrics.criterion: The per-worker record's restored members do not entangle it with engine state: they operate on the record's own data (plus ordinary arguments like a result object or elapsed seconds), without reaching into controller/controller-owned attributes such as resume tables, shutdown flags, thread layout or the engine's hit stack.
rubrics.rationale: The natural botch here is moving the consumer-report loop wholesale onto the record; that would trade engine-reaches-data envy for record-reaches-engine envy, keeping the same coupling in the opposite direction.

rubrics.criterion: The decision of which indicator/row variant applies (for example, plain timing-only results versus results exposing content length) is made by the owning class in one place, and the repaired code contains no second, differently-styled discriminator between response kinds in the reporting path.
rubrics.rationale: The displaced implementation deliberately grew two styles of variant probing (an explicit subclass branch and a feature probe) in two separate helpers; eliminating the duplicated variant knowledge is a material part of restoring ownership, not a stylistic preference.

rubrics.criterion: The module-level support functions that the reported centralization added to serve the logging pipeline (the row-building and indicator-tuple helpers next to the log service) are removed or reduced to thin delegations in the same change, so no free functions remain that unpack response fields themselves.
rubrics.rationale: Leaving those helpers in place as dead code (or as a parallel implementation still reading foreign fields) would keep exactly the displaced behavior the task asks to relocate, just one hop away.

rubrics.criterion: The engine methods that previously held the displaced implementations (the response-condition dispatch on the controller and the three progress-reading/writing/rendering methods) are deleted or fully repurposed in the same change, leaving no dead engine-side duplicates of the relocated behavior.
rubrics.rationale: The displaced engine methods are obsolete once behavior returns to its owners; retaining them forces every future reader to reconcile two implementations of the same duty inside the single production module.

rubrics.criterion: No uncalled definitions, unused imports or other dead markers are left behind by the relocation anywhere in the production module (every member the change touched either has a live caller or is gone).
rubrics.rationale: Single-module codebases rot fastest through orphaned members; the instance's cleanup obligation includes what the relocation itself orphans, not just the helpers it displaced.

rubrics.criterion: Every declared condition still means exactly what it meant before for the kinds that support it: anchored status matching, inclusive ranges for sizes and timings (and for content length where declared), exact message equality for the message condition, substring and regular-expression message search with each kind's existing multiline behavior, and no operator silently extended to kinds that did not support it.
rubrics.rationale: The condition dispatch was relocated wholesale in this instance; anchors, range endpoints and per-kind message-search modes are the behavioral edge most easily lost or blurred in a hand-rewrite of that dispatch.

rubrics.criterion: Requesting a condition a response kind does not support, or a condition name that does not exist, still fails the way it did before — an AttributeError naming the unavailable match_<condition> for the response's actual class — and that failure is not swallowed into a special verdict.
rubrics.rationale: The engine's per-condition dispatch in this instance encodes both unsupported-kind and unknown-key failures as class-shaped AttributeError text; preserving them keeps operator diagnostics and the free/skip action contract stable.

rubrics.criterion: Progress accounting keeps its exact transitions: a skip advances the skip count only; a retry leaves the attempt open; hit/fail/ignore advance the done count exactly once with hits/failures counted on their own paths; a quit report sets the shared shutdown flag; and resume arithmetic plus the recent-seconds timing ring produce the same values as before.
rubrics.rationale: The consumer-report loop was the most entangled site in this instance; moving counter transitions onto the record is precisely where a rewrite could reorder done-count increments, drop the retry path's early return, or mis-index the seconds ring.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not strand any response kind: restored evaluation and presentation behavior must be reachable for plain result objects, not only for the result subclass that carries content length (and not only via code that assumes every response is that subclass).
rubrics.rationale: The most tempting mechanical repair in this instance — moving the displaced functions verbatim onto the content-length subclass — makes plain result objects lose evaluation and dump naming entirely, which is the highest-probability silent breakage a grader must catch.
